messages.subject: Multy state model
parts:
Hello all, 
I am working on a multi state model, based on:  
Kéry, M., & Schaub, M. (2011). Bayesian population analysis using WinBUGS: a hierarchical perspective. Academic Press. Section 10.3.2.
It is a basic model that has the state process defined as: "Not yet entered", "young", "adult", "dead". 
And the observation process is: "seen as young", "seen as adult", "not seen".
The model works as data augmentation, on a simulated population. It is of my interest, so estimate the total population size of the individuals. Coding and estimation procedure are similar as in the book, but the outcomes are somehow curious for me. Let me explain

My final posterior distributions  for the total population size seems to make sense, and is closed to the true, value. But when I study the population size at each time point, t=1 gives me a trace-plot that is a straight line, where the value is equal to the number of sampled individuals. 
The model keeps underestimating all values for the population size at different time points. and in the final time point, it overestimate the population size, in order to guess the correct value of the Total Population size. 

Is this normal in this kind of models ? how can I make sure that the posterior distribution of the different time points works better with the Data augmentation and have a better estimation? 

Any other thoughts are welcome. If you consider that I need to share the code to make it more informative, I will happily do it. 

Thank you in advance :) 
--
Diego Rondon

messages.author: 312eda23f89ab6c6
messages.subject: AW: Multy state model
parts:
Hi Diego,

If you get a straight line for the number of individual at the occasion when individuals are encountered for the first time, this means that the recruitment is deterministic, which is obviously not what you wanted to have. Have you included a single recruitment parameter? And if so, for you young individuals only, or only for the adults? If you could share the code, this would help to (potentially) see where the problem is.

Kind regards

Michael

messages.author: 238422c6037ad1c9
messages.subject: Re: Multy state model
parts:
Hello, 
yes, sorry for that missing part.
there are some lines of codes, that do the following transformation
When the individual is first see, it is marked as 1, after that all other encounters are mark as adult.
for example: 01101 will be 01202 (not see, seen young, seen adult, not seen, seen adult).
To avoid issues with the 0 label, I just do +1 in all the numbers, in a way that:
  • not yet enter=1
  • seen young =2
  • seen adult=4
  • dead=4

The column with the decimal number, holds information related to the "inbreeding level" of the individual, and it letter helps to model the survival probability.
The final column, it is just the identification number for the individual. 

I hope is clear
--
Diego Rondon
